[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Dimensionality Reduction: PCA, t-SNE, and UMAP Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"High-dimensional data is a common challenge in data science. As the number of features grows, models often suffer from the curse of dimensionality, leading to overfitting and high computational costs. Dimensionality reduction techniques help project high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional space while retaining meaningful underlying structure."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Principal Component Analysis (PCA)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"PCA is a linear dimensionality reduction technique that maximizes variance. It identifies orthogonal axes, called principal components, along which the variation of the data is maximized. PCA is fast, deterministic, and widely used for data preprocessing and noise reduction."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris

# Load dataset
data = load_iris()
X = data.data
y = data.target

# Initialize and fit PCA
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X)

print("Original shape:", X.shape)
print("Reduced shape:", X_pca.shape)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"t-SNE is a non-linear technique particularly well-suited for the visualization of high-dimensional datasets. It converts similarities between data points to joint probabilities and minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the low-dimensional and high-dimensional representations. Note that t-SNE is non-deterministic and can be computationally expensive."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.manifold import TSNE

# Initialize and fit t-SNE
# perplexity is a crucial hyperparameter to tune
tsne = TSNE(n_components=2, perplexity=30.0, random_state=42)
X_tsne = tsne.fit_transform(X)

print("t-SNE reduced shape:", X_tsne.shape)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"UMAP is a newer non-linear dimensionality reduction technique based on Riemannian geometry and algebraic topology. It often preserves both local and global structure better than t-SNE and scales exceptionally well to larger datasets while maintaining faster execution times."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Requires umap-learn package: pip install umap-learn
import umap

# Initialize and fit UMAP
reducer = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, random_state=42)
X_umap = reducer.fit_transform(X)

print("UMAP reduced shape:", X_umap.shape)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary and Best Practices"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use PCA when you need a fast, linear transformation, feature extraction for downstream machine learning models, or maximum variance preservation."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use t-SNE when your primary goal is 2D or 3D cluster visualization and capturing local neighborhoods, keeping in mind it does not preserve global distances well."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use UMAP as a modern alternative to t-SNE when you need faster computation, better scalability, and preservation of both local and global data topology."}]
